title: The universal affine translation has a natural unit multiplier
statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible, where Noetherian means having a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $d\geq0$, put $P=\mathbf A^d_S$, $W=\mathbf A^d_P$, and let $q_P:W\to P$ and $p:P\to S$ be the projections [def-sbc-affine-space]. The zero section $e:S\to P$ is given by all coordinates zero. Let $\tau:W\to W$ be $(z,a)\mapsto(z-a,a)$, an automorphism over $P$ with inverse $(z,a)\mapsto(z+a,a)$. Work in the ordinary etale derived categories of $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and put $L_P=A_W(d)[2d]$ using the canonical Tate pullback maps [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. With ordinary compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support], let $M_P=Rq_{P!}L_P$, let $t_P:M_P\xrightarrow{\sim}A_P[0]$ be the normalized coordinate-tower trace [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], and let $\rho_P=Rq_{P!}(\kappa_\tau)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau}$ be the canonical action [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change], with its bounded-below exchange interpreted in the unbounded category by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons].

There is a unique section $b\in\Gamma(P,A_P)^\times$ of the constant etale coefficient sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] such that the equality of actual derived morphisms is
$$t_P\circ\rho_P\circ t_P^{-1}=m_b[0],$$
where $m_b:A_P\to A_P$ is multiplication by $b$. Under the canonical section/function identification [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], $b$ is a Zariski-locally constant function $|P|\to A^\times$. For every morphism $u:T\to P$ with $T$ Noetherian, form $W_T=W\times_PT$, the translated action $\rho_T$ on $M_T=Rq_{T!}A_{W_T}(d)[2d]$, and the normalized trace $t_T:M_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T[0]$ by the same constructions. For the canonical exchange $C_u:u^*M_P\xrightarrow{\sim}M_T$, one has
$$C_u\circ u^*\rho_P=\rho_T\circ C_u,\qquad t_T\circ C_u=u^*t_P,\qquad t_T\circ\rho_T\circ t_T^{-1}=m_{u^*b}[0].$$
In particular $e^*b=1$: under zero-section pullback the action is $\rho_{1,1}=1$ with the canonical identity Tate identification.

proof.text: Apply [def-amb-affine-trace-tower] over $S$, $P$ and every Noetherian $T$ in the statement. Its coordinate identifications give $W_T=\mathbf A^d_T$, separated finite-type projections, Noetherian total spaces, and invertibility of $N$ on all stages. The finite affine Noetherian covers give quasi-compactness, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] gives quasi-separatedness. Choose compactifications by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Their open parts are quasi-compact: the inverse image of an affine open of the middle scheme is an open of the Noetherian source, hence quasi-compact. For this last implication apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] to complements of finite unions in a covering of the open: a minimal complement cannot meet another member of the cover, so that finite union covers the open. The polynomial formulas $z\mapsto z-a$ and $z\mapsto z+a$ are inverse over $P$, including $d=0$.

source.place: Step 1: translation, action on the coefficient line

proof.text: The object $L_P=A_W(d)[2d]$ is bounded below. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], $\kappa_\tau:\tau^*L_P\cong L_P$ is an isomorphism, and its pullback to $W_T$ is the specified $\kappa_{\tau_T}$, using the composition comparison. Apply [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] with $(f,a,K,\theta)=(q_P,\tau,L_P,\kappa_\tau)$: it gives the automorphism $\rho_P$ in the statement. By [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], $t_P$ is an isomorphism. The bounded-below normalizations of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identify these very maps with their unbounded versions. Thus $\alpha=t_P\rho_Pt_P^{-1}$ is an automorphism of $A_P[0]$.

source.place: Step 1: translation, action on the coefficient line

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to the abelian category of $A_P$-module sheaves. There are unique sheaf endomorphisms $h,k:A_P\to A_P$ with $h[0]=\alpha$ and $k[0]=\alpha^{-1}$. Functoriality and injectivity on Hom give $hk=kh=1$. These are sheaf maps lifting the actual derived morphisms, not merely their actions on global cohomology.

Set $b=h_P(1)$ and $c=k_P(1)$ in $\Gamma(P,A_P)$. For any etale object $U\to P$ and any section $x\in A_P(U)$, $A_P$-linearity and restriction compatibility give $h_U(x)=h_U(x\cdot1)=x h_U(1)=x b|_U$, and likewise $k_U(x)=x c|_U$. Hence $h=m_b$, $k=m_c$, and $hk=kh=1$ evaluated at $1$ gives $bc=cb=1$. Thus $b$ is a unit and $\alpha=m_b[0]$. Any other multiplier has the same sheaf map by the injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], and evaluation at $1$ gives the same section. This proves existence and uniqueness.

source.place: Step 1: translation, action on the coefficient line

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] to the additive group of $A$. The sections $b,c$ become Zariski-locally constant functions to $A$. On each open on which both are constant, the equation $bc=1$ says that the value of $b$ lies in $A^\times$. These opens cover $P$, so the same function is locally constant with codomain $A^\times$. The section/function identification respects multiplication here: restrict to these constant opens, multiply the constant values, and use the sheaf equality axiom.

For $u:T\to P$, [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] gives $C_u u^*\rho_P=\rho_T C_u$, since the Tate isomorphisms pull back as checked in step 2. The trace lemma [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] gives $t_T C_u=u^*t_P$. Both equations use the same exchange by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Inserting $C_u^{-1}C_u$ and these equations gives
$$t_T\rho_Tt_T^{-1}=(u^*t_P)(u^*\rho_P)(u^*t_P)^{-1}=u^*(t_P\rho_Pt_P^{-1})=u^*(m_b[0]).$$
By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], inverse image preserves the constant ring, multiplication and $1$, and is exact. Applying it to the formula $x\mapsto bx$ gives $u^*m_b=m_{u^*b}$ on sheaves; applying it termwise to the degree-zero complexes gives $m_{u^*b}[0]$. No flatness or finite-type assumption on $u$ is needed.

source.place: Step 1: translation, action on the coefficient line

proof.text: Take $u=e:S\to P$. All translation parameters become zero, so $\tau_e=1_{\mathbf A^d_S}$. The identity and composition normalization of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] makes $\kappa_{\tau_e}$ the identity. Thus [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] gives $\rho_{1,1}=1$. Step 6 implies $m_{e^*b}[0]=t_S1t_S^{-1}=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], $m_{e^*b}=1$ as a sheaf map; evaluation at $1$ proves $e^*b=1$.
